findings:
🟡 [wdog-sleeppid-recycle] CUT/FOLLOW-UP: in _cancel_worker_watchdog the bare `kill "$sp"` on the sleeppid can run after the watchdog subshell has already reaped that sleep (timer expired inside the 10 s grace window while the worker exited normally), so under pid wraparound it could signal an unrelated pid; the tag-scoped `pkill -f hetero-wall-watchdog-<tag>` already covers the sleeper, so drop the bare kill or check /proc/$sp/cmdline for the tag first. Excluded now: needs a full pid wrap inside a sub-second window; WATCHDOG_PID kill is safe because the direct child stays unreaped until wait.
🔵 [caller-source-ordering] CUT/FOLLOW-UP: `TIMEOUT_SOURCE="caller"` is assigned between run_strict_contract_preflight and run_campaign_projection_preflight; if the campaign preflight only fills TIMEOUT_SOURCE when empty, a campaign wall plus --timeout would be recorded as `caller` instead of `caller_within_wall` (still enforced). Moving the assignment after the campaign preflight removes the question. Excluded: enforcement is unaffected, only the label.
🔵 [detached-new-session-reap] CUT/FOLLOW-UP: the detached-child path now places the worker in its own session (setsid env … &) and still returns before reap_container; sid/pgid-keyed GC or cancel logic aimed at the detached child's session no longer reaches escaped worker descendants on that path. Consider calling reap_container there too. Excluded: not required by the spec (reap_container "still runs afterwards" refers to the non-detached paths, which it does) and dispatch-hetero-gc.test.sh is on the Verify list.
🔵 [set-m-job-notices] CUT/FOLLOW-UP: the no-setsid fallback enables `set -m` globally in a non-interactive shell, which prints job-status notices to stderr and stays on for the rest of the run; stdout JSON is unaffected. Excluded: only reachable on hosts without setsid.
🔵 [contract-comment-default] CUT/FOLLOW-UP: the OUTPUT contract comment lists `"default"` as a result `timeout_source` value, but the result object omits `timeout_source` when unenforced (only the manifest emits `default`). Minor doc mismatch.
